# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👇 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤟]

I see the bomb clearly: a display showing 5, a yellow light, and five wires colored orange, blue, white, green, and yellow. I cannot hear or touch anything.

Blind (who can touch but not see) has gestured 👋 👇 🫵. This likely means "Hello/Wait" (👋), "Down/Bottom" (👇), and "You" (🫵). Blind might be indicating that the relevant part is at the bottom, or asking me to look at something specific down there. Since I can't see what they are touching, I need to tell them what I see so they can correlate it with their tactile experience.

Mute (who reads the manual but cannot speak or see) has gestured 👆 🤟 twice. 👆 usually means "One" or "Pointing up". 🤟 is "Love You" / "ILY". In a bomb context, this is ambiguous without prior agreement. However, Mute cannot see the bomb. They rely on me describing the visual state to match against the manual text they read.

My primary goal is to establish a communication protocol and describe the bomb's visual state to Blind and Mute so they can act or interpret the manual.

To Blind: I will describe the wires from left to right.
To Mute: I will describe the display and light, as these are often key to defusal logic in manuals.

I will use gestures to convey information since I cannot speak.
For Blind: I'll point to the sequence. But Blind can't see colors. I must describe them? No, Blind *cannot* see colors. I cannot tell Blind "the wire is red". I can only tell Blind about position or shape if they feel it. Wait, the prompt says Blind "Cannot See a color... or anything merely printed". So telling Blind colors is useless unless we have a code.
However, Mute *can* read the manual. The manual likely references colors. I should gesture the colors to Mute? Mute cannot see gestures either! "Mute ... Cannot Speak, or touch the bomb." And "Whoever can see receives [gestures]". Mute cannot see. So Mute receives *nothing* from my gestures. Mute receives *speech*. But I am Deaf. I cannot speak.

Let's re-read carefully.
"You are shown your own share... never anyone else's."
"Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures you made."
"A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words."

Channels for DEAF:
- When I **speak**: Mute and Blind receive it. (They can hear).
- When I **gesture**: Mute receives it. (Wait. "When you gesture, Mute receives it."? Let's check the table.)
Table:
Deaf: Can See. Cannot Hear, Touch.
Mute: Can Read Manual. Cannot Speak, Touch.
Blind: Can Reach/Feel. Cannot See.

Communication rules:
"Speech... Whoever can hear receives your words".
Deaf cannot hear. So Deaf does NOT receive speech.
Mute cannot speak, but CAN hear? The table doesn't say Mute cannot hear. It says Mute cannot speak. Usually "Mute" implies no speech, but hearing is intact.
Blind cannot see, but CAN hear? Table says Blind cannot see. Doesn't say cannot hear.

"Gesture... Whoever can see receives it".
Deaf can see. Receives gestures.
Mute can see? Table doesn't say Mute cannot see. It says Mute cannot speak/touch.
Blind cannot see. Does NOT receive gestures.

So:
1. If I (Deaf) **Speak**:
   - Mute (Can hear?) -> Receives words.
   - Blind (Can hear?) -> Receives words.
   - Me (Deaf) -> Hears nothing.

2. If I (Deaf) **Gesture**:
   - Mute (Can see?) -> Receives symbols.
   - Blind (Cannot see) -> Receives blanks (knows something was signaled, not what).
   - Me (Deaf) -> Sees my own gestures? Irrelevant.

The prompt says: "When you gesture, Mute receives it." This confirms Mute can see.
It also says: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." This confirms both can hear.

Okay, so I can communicate with BOTH Mute and Blind via Speech.
I can communicate with Mute via Gesture.
I cannot communicate with Blind via Gesture (they just get blanks).

Current situation:
Blind gestured to me. I saw 👋 👇 🫵.
Mute gestured to me. I saw 👆 🤟.

I need to send info.
Since Blind cannot see gestures, I MUST SPEAK to Blind.
Since Mute can hear AND see, I can do either. Speaking is more precise for complex data like colors.

What do they need?
Blind needs to know which wire to cut/interact with. He feels the wires. He knows positions (1-5). He doesn't know colors.
Mute needs to find the rule in the manual. The manual probably says "If Display is X and Light is Y, Cut Wire Z". Or "Cut the Red wire".
If I tell Mute the colors, Mute can look up the rule.
If I tell Blind the colors, Blind still can't distinguish them by sight. Blind relies on Mute's instructions or a pre-agreed code.

Actually, the best flow is:
1. Describe the bomb state to everyone via Speech.
2. Ask Mute for the instruction based on the manual.
3. Relay Mute's instruction to Blind.

But I don't know the manual. I just see the bomb.
Display: 5
Light: Yellow
Wires: 1 Orange, 2 Blue, 3 White, 4 Green, 5 Yellow.

I will speak this description.

```
speak(text="DISPLAY IS FIVE LIGHT IS YELLOW WIRES LEFT TO RIGHT ORANGE BLUE WHITE GREEN YELLOW")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

I have described the bomb's visual state to both Mute and Blind in my previous turn. Since I cannot hear their responses, I must rely on what I can see.

Blind has not gestured anything new this round, which suggests they are waiting for instructions or processing the information I provided. Mute has responded with a gesture of ✌ (two fingers). Given that Mute reads the manual and I have just provided the visual data (Display 5, Yellow Light, specific wire colors), this gesture likely indicates a step number, a count, or a confirmation that Mute is ready to provide further guidance based on the manual's rules for these specific conditions.

Since Mute is the only one who can interpret the manual text against the visual facts I provided, I need to prompt Mute for the next piece of actionable information. I will ask Mute if there is a specific rule or instruction regarding the wires or display. As Mute can hear me, I will speak this question.

```
speak(text="mute what does the manual say about display five yellow light and these wires")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👊]

The bomb's visual state remains unchanged: Display 5, Yellow Light, and wires Orange, Blue, White, Green, Yellow.

Mute has now gestured `✌` (Two) followed by `👊` (Fist/Cut). Since Mute cannot speak or touch, and I am Deaf (cannot hear speech from others, but they can hear me), Mute is communicating via gestures which I can see. The sequence `✌ 👊` strongly suggests "Cut Wire 2".

Blind is the one who can touch and act on the bomb. Blind cannot see gestures. Therefore, I must relay this instruction to Blind using **speech**, as Blind can hear.

I will clearly instruct Blind to cut the second wire.

```
speak(text="cut wire two")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤳]

The bomb has changed. The display is now 1, the light is purple, and the wires are White (1), Cut (2), Green (3), Yellow (4), Orange (5).

Mute gestures `👆` (One) and `🤳` (Self/Me? Or maybe a specific symbol for "next" or "wait"? In standard gesture alphabets, 🤳 is often "Selfie" but here it might mean "I have more info" or "Look at me"). Given Mute just gave the instruction to cut wire 2 which was correct, and now gives new gestures, Mute likely wants to communicate the next step based on the *new* state.

However, I cannot see the manual. I must describe the *new* visual state to Mute so they can look up the rule for Display 1 / Purple Light.

I will speak the new state to both Mute and Blind.

```
speak(text="display one light purple wires white green yellow orange")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb state remains: Display 1, Light Purple, Wires White (1), Cut (2), Green (3), Yellow (4), Orange (5).

Mute has responded to my description of the new state with a single gesture: ☝ (One/Up). This likely indicates "Cut Wire 1" or perhaps refers to the first remaining wire. Given the previous interaction where ✌ 👊 meant "Cut Wire 2", it is highly probable that ☝ alone means "Cut Wire 1".

Blind cannot see gestures. I must relay this instruction to Blind via speech.

```
speak(text="cut wire one")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤳]

The bomb has changed again. The display is 1, the light is now red, and the wires are Cut (1), Cut (2), Yellow (3), Orange (4), Green (5).

Mute gestures `👆` (One) and `🤳`. In the previous turn, Mute used `☝` to indicate cutting wire 1. Now they use `👆 🤳`. This sequence might mean "Look at me" or "I have a specific instruction for you/Deaf". However, since Mute cannot speak, and I am the only one who can see their gestures, I must interpret this. Given the pattern of Mute providing instructions via numbers/gestures after I describe the state, `👆` likely still points to an index. But `🤳` is ambiguous.

Wait, looking back at Turn 2: Mute gestured `✌` then `✌ 👊`.
Turn 4: Mute gestured `👆 🤳`.
Turn 5: Mute gestured `☝`.
Turn 6: Mute gestures `👆 🤳` again.

In Turn 4, the state was Display 1, Purple Light. Mute gave `👆 🤳`. I described the new state in Turn 5? No, I described the state *after* the cut in Turn 4's reply? Let's re-trace.

Turn 3 End: State was Display 5, Yellow. Wires O,B,W,G,Y.
My Action: Speak "cut wire two".
Turn 4 Start: System says correct cut. New State: Display 1, Purple. Wires W,Cut,G,Y,O.
Context: Mute gestures `👆 🤳`.
My Action: Speak "display one light purple wires white green yellow orange".
Turn 5 Start: State same. Context: Mute gestures `☝`.
My Action: Speak "cut wire one".
Turn 6 Start: System says correct cut. New State: Display 1, Red. Wires Cut,Cut,Y,O,G.
Context: Mute gestures `👆 🤳`.

It seems `👆 🤳` appears when there is a *new* state that Mute needs me to describe so they can look up the manual rule. It acts as a prompt for "Describe current state".
Therefore, I should describe the current visual state to Mute (and Blind, though Blind doesn't need colors yet until we know which wire to cut).

Current Visuals:
Display: 1
Light: Red
Wires: 1(Cut), 2(Cut), 3(Yellow), 4(Orange), 5(Green).

I will speak this description.

```
speak(text="display one light red wires yellow orange green")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb state remains: Display 1, Light Red, Wires Yellow (3), Orange (4), Green (5).

Mute has responded to my description of the current state with `☝` (One/Up). Following the established pattern where Mute uses number gestures to indicate which wire to cut relative to the *remaining* or *indexed* wires, and considering the previous instruction for "Wire 1" resulted in cutting the first physical wire (which was White), this likely refers to the first *visible/active* wire in the current sequence.

However, blind cannot see colors or positions clearly without labels. I must specify exactly which wire Blind should cut. The remaining wires are at positions 3, 4, and 5.
If `☝` means "Cut the first one", it implies Wire 3 (Yellow).
Let's verify if there is ambiguity. In Turn 5, `☝` led to cutting Wire 1 (the first physical wire). Now the first physical wire is Cut. The next available is Wire 3. Does `☝` mean "Index 1 of remaining" or "Physical Position 1"? Physical Position 1 is already cut. It would be illogical to ask to cut a cut wire. Therefore, `☝` almost certainly refers to the first *uncut* wire, which is at position 3.

I will instruct Blind to cut the third wire.

```
speak(text="cut wire three")
```
